answer: Agents lock a stake bond to earn audit rights, and each epoch a verifiable random draw picks a small committee, so an attacker cannot aim fake identities at one target and must instead own a large slice of all stake. Committee members whisper signed receipts through a gossip layer before they settle into the shared reef of state; a Sybil flood entering by any inlet fails cross-checks, and correlated slashing burns the whole bond, so each extra fake node raises the attacker cost.
